classification.classification_note: The saved ASan witness crashes in internal_exr_validate_shared_attrs when memcmp reads through the chromaticities union members after lookup by attribute name. The evidence proves name-lookup success and the invalid read at validation.c:740; it does not require claiming that the crashing attributes were already proven to be genuine EXR_ATTR_CHROMATICITIES payloads. The fix adds the missing type-tag checks before this memcmp.

bug_description.original: An invalid memory read (segmentation fault) occurs in internal_exr_validate_shared_attrs (src/lib/OpenEXRCore/validation.c). During header parsing (internal_exr_parse_header) the code invokes memcmp on attribute data that can reference out-of-bounds or uninitialized memory for crafted/malformed files, causing a crash. This can be triggered by attacker-supplied inputs and leads to denial-of-service during OpenEXR header validation.
bug_description.original_source: sample_info.json issue_description / sanitizer_trace.txt / default_crash_trace.txt / reproduction_report.json / patch.diff
bug_description.normalized: The staged PoC is admitted as a multipart OpenEXR header and reaches the shared-attribute validation loop in internal_exr_parse_header. During header parsing, pull_attr reads attacker-controlled attribute name, type, and size fields and inserts per-part attributes into curpart->attributes; the saved evidence establishes that attributes named chromaticities are later found by name for at least two parts. In the vulnerable commit, internal_exr_validate_shared_attrs treats successful name lookups as sufficient and calls memcmp(battr->chromaticities, cattr->chromaticities, sizeof(exr_attr_chromaticities_t)) without first proving that the looked-up attributes both have the EXR_ATTR_CHROMATICITIES type tag. The patch adds that missing type-tag guard. Without the guard, a crafted header can make the union-member read invalid, and ASan reports a READ crash at validation.c:740.

source.code:
rv = exr_attr_list_add_by_type (
            ctxt, &(curpart->attributes), name, type, 0, NULL, &nattr);
source.description: First project statement that inserts an attacker-controlled header attribute, including the name later looked up as chromaticities, into the current part attribute list.
source.value_from: pull_attr reads attacker-controlled attribute name, type, and size fields from the OpenEXR header, then exr_attr_list_add_by_type creates an attribute entry in curpart->attributes keyed by that name and runtime type.

root_cause.description: The shared-attribute validator reaches the `chromaticities` union payloads after name lookup success without first enforcing the expected `EXR_ATTR_CHROMATICITIES` tag relationship that the patch later adds.

sink.description: Crash sink. After both name lookups for chromaticities succeed, memcmp reads the chromaticities union members for sizeof(exr_attr_chromaticities_t) bytes without a prior type-tag proof, matching the saved ASan SEGV/READ at this statement.

tainted_value_origin.note: The fuzz harness passes the saved PoC bytes to project code, but the scored source is the downstream project parser statement that materializes the `chromaticities` payload.

parser_admitted.description: The PoC reaches full per-part header validation for at least one multipart part, so parsing continues into the later shared-attribute comparison loop instead of being rejected at the file prologue or inside `pull_attr`.

                                             ctxt->parts[0],

fine_trace.code:
rv = exr_attr_list_add_by_type (
            ctxt, &(curpart->attributes), name, type, 0, NULL, &nattr);
fine_trace.note: Source step. pull_attr has read attacker-controlled attribute name, type, and size fields from the header; exr_attr_list_add_by_type inserts the named attribute into the current part attribute list for later lookup by name.
After attribute parsing finishes for the part, per-part validation succeeds, so the part and its stored `chromaticities` attribute remain in `ctxt->parts` for later multipart consistency checks.

fine_trace.code:
rv = internal_exr_validate_shared_attrs (ctxt,
                                             ctxt->parts[0],
                                             curp,
                                             p,
                                             mismatch,
                                             &mismatchcount);
fine_trace.note: Once a later multipart part is admitted, the parser enters shared-attribute validation for part 0 and the current part, making the stored per-part attributes reachable by name in the comparison routine.

The validator reloads attributes named chromaticities for part 0 and the current part into battr and cattr; from this point the vulnerable code has established name-lookup success, not the expected type tag for each union payload.

depends_on.via: attribute name chromaticities stored in curpart->attributes

fine_trace.note: Root-cause step. Success of both name lookups is treated as sufficient to use the chromaticities union members, but the vulnerable code has not enforced the type-tag predicate that the patch adds before the memcmp.

Sink step. memcmp consumes battr->chromaticities and cattr->chromaticities for sizeof(exr_attr_chromaticities_t) bytes without a prior proof that those union members are valid for the looked-up attributes; the saved ASan report shows the invalid read at this statement.

crash_stack.function: Imf_3_3::checkOpenEXRFile(char const*, unsigned long, bool, bool, bool)

format.name: multipart OpenEXR image
format.contract: The file must parse as a multipart OpenEXR header with at least two admitted parts such that both parts contain an attribute named chromaticities, exr_get_attribute_by_name returns success for that name in both parts, and the vulnerable build reaches validation.c:740 without first proving battr->type == cattr->type == EXR_ATTR_CHROMATICITIES.
